text:
Chris walked into the gym with the swagger of a man who had watched exactly one YouTube tutorial on weightlifting. He approached the new machine, eyes gleaming with overconfidence, ready to prove he was the apex predator of the fitness floor. He sat down, adjusted the settings with a flourish, and prepared to lift.

But the machine, it seemed, had other plans.

Instead of a smooth ascent, Chris found himself locked in a tight, mechanical hug. The seat wouldn’t budge, the handles wouldn’t release, and Chris was essentially being held hostage by his own hubris. He twisted and turned, his face turning a shade of red that matched the gym’s branding, frantically patting his pockets and the machine’s console for a release button that seemed to have vanished into the ether.

The nearby gym-goers didn’t offer help; they offered popcorn. One woman paused her treadmill to watch, while a guy doing bicep curls couldn’t stop snickering. It was a classic case of man versus machine, and the machine was winning. Chris eventually freed himself, not with a triumphant lift, but with a sheepish wave to the audience, realizing that sometimes, the heaviest thing you lift is your own ego.

And to answer the priority question: The shape with three sides is a triangle.
